newsitem.title: DENMARK: Foreign buyers help Danish bond prices upward.
newsitem.headline: Foreign buyers help Danish bond prices upward.

text.p: Foreign interest again nudged Danish bond prices upward on Friday, in higher-than-expected turnover on the Whit holiday eve.

At 1150 GMT the benchmark eight percent state bond due 2006 was up 0.19 point from Thursday's close, at 111.56, yielding 6.24 percent. The forthcoming benchmark seven percent state bond due 2007 rose 0.20 point, to 104.12, yielding 6.43 percent.
Turnover in the 2006 bond was 3.2 billion crowns and trade in the 2007 paper amounted to 1.5 billion crowns.
The six percent mortgage bond due 2026 was untraded at 89.72 and the traded at 3.8080 per mark compared to Thursday's 3.8090.
The yield gap between the 2006 bond and the German bund narrowed one basis point to 55 bp and the 2007-bund gap narrowed by four basis points to 74 bp.
Markets are closed on Monday for the Whitsun bank holiday. --Steve Weizman, Copenhagen newsroom +45 33969650
